# natural-structural fixtures — provenance

Generated by `natgen.py` / `genfix.py` (kept with the worker, not shipped), authored
directly from `docs/design/storage-format.md` §1, §6, §7.2 and §7.5 — **not** from the
Rust encoder under test. `CASES.json` records each case's event tag, byte length and
SHA-256.

Gate applied before any fixture was trusted: the same generator reproduces the accepted
`format-contract/DELIVERY-10` bytes exactly —
`golden.genesis.tx.sgl` Genesis (271 B) plus its nine `IdAllocation` events (40 B each),
and `golden.v3.tx.sgl` KbMetadataUpdated (254 B), IdAllocation (40 B) and
RequestOutcomeRecorded (191 B). `genesis-accepted.hex` **is** that accepted Genesis event.

Consequence: an expected image here cannot inherit a symmetric width/order error from the
encoder it checks. `cases` are immutable inputs; adding one is a new file, never an edit.

No `/tmp` path is required at test time: tests read only files in this directory and fail
(rather than skip) when a mandatory fixture is absent.

## v2 correction — event 192, coordinator ruling (iii), 2026-11-17

`outcome-min.hex` was regenerated. v1 encoded `actor_origin = 2` (unavailable) with tag 5
absent and was accepted; under ruling (iii) that image is **illegal**, because row 192
lists `5 recorded_by` in 专属必现 and the event is the only one of the 30 whose row does so.

| fixture | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| `outcome-min` | origin 2, no tag 5 (164 B) | origin 1, tag 5 present (184 B, `8cf4accc…`) |
| `outcome-legacy-with-five` | — | new: origin 1 + tag 5, the conjunction's other positive arm (227 B, `620d9a0d…`) |

The v1 bytes are preserved, not deleted: `evidence/preimage-v1-final192/` holds the v1
`natural.rs`, `natural_codec.rs` and every v1 fixture with its own hash list. The v1 image
now functions as a **negative** case in `natural_codec.rs`.

Constants, ordering and every other fixture are unchanged; the generator gate still
reproduces the accepted DELIVERY-10 bytes. Both 192 vectors remain independently authored
from the spec tables, never from the encoder under test.
